question: How do production agent systems stop an agent asserting false success, so The Architect stops making statements to the founder that are false?
decision_fed: The Architect truth gate: validate structured claims against the existing verification_evidence.db ledger instead of grading outbound prose; merge-track upstream hermes-agent issue #54722 / PR #54738 which is this exact gate, rather than writing a second one (LAW 3).
findings: False success is a measured failure class: 44-52% of all failures on tau2-bench, 75.8% on AppWorld, per-model 13-89% (arXiv 2606.09863). Receipt-checking against a runtime-written ledger detects 91% at 4% false positives versus 35% for regex word-lists (arXiv 2603.10060) — the word-list approach this estate already banned as proxy-grading is also the measurably losing one. Deterministic checks first (claim carries an evidence event id that must exist in SQLite with exit 0 and a timestamp after the last mutation), factored verifier model only for what the ledger cannot type. Upstream hermes-agent has the gate in flight: issue #54722, PR #54738.
metric: Share of outbound Architect status claims carrying a valid evidence event id; false-success rate on a replayed claim set.
metric_before: 0% of claims evidence-linked; live verification_evidence.db has 0 events; verify_on_stop OFF on the founder's only surface (Telegram).

question: What experience-accumulation patterns measurably make an agent improve, so maestro and The Architect learn fast with proof?
decision_fed: Maestro consult-before-escalate: fingerprint each problem, replay the last successful fix for a matching fingerprint before escalating, and a weekly learning receipt to Telegram proving what last week's escalations cost this week. Distill failures as well as successes (ReasoningBank result); promote a fix to a skill only after 2+ successful reuses.
findings: Distilled strategy memory from successes AND failures beats raw episodic memory: up to +34.2% effectiveness, -16% steps (ReasoningBank, arXiv 2509.25140). Skill libraries reach milestones 8.5-15.3x faster (Voyager). Proof of learning that survives workload drift: a frozen replay set of ~20 real past incidents re-run weekly — solved-count trend is the one metric immune to the workload changing under you. The everyday metrics: repeat-incident escalation rate declining, repeat resolution time versus first occurrence, memory hit rate.
metric: Weekly learning receipt: fraction of last week's escalation fingerprints auto-resolved this week; repeat-incident median resolution time versus first occurrence; frozen replay set solved-count.
metric_before: maestro consults nothing before escalating; one Stripe finding escalated 46 times in 29h with zero learning between passes; skills/shapes tables held 0 rows until PR #4.
